title: Shared-wrapper (table protocol) for aliased blob write params
impact: [Exp 234](234-blob-param-transfer.md) wraps each large blob write param in its own `TransferableTypedData`, but walked param positions independently — a caller handing the **same** `Uint8List` object to N positions (or reusing one buffer across a coalesced `MultiExecuteRequest` burst) got N separate `fromList` copies of one buffer, a latent regression that is strictly worse than the graph copy exp 234 replaced. Exp 243 wraps by **identity**: an identity-keyed cache shares **one** wrapper per unique backing buffer (`cache[value] ??= fromList([value])`), referenced at every occurrence; the graph copier sends it once (identity preserved), and `unwrapBlobParams` materializes each wrapper exactly once (a shared unwrap cache spans the coalesced envelope's writes, since a second `materialize()` throws). Isolated transport of one 300 KB buffer referenced N times shows the table protocol **flat and fastest at every N** (32.9/27.0/28.2/33.8/56.5 µs at N=1/2/4/8/32) where the two alternatives each fail differently: the exp 234 **baseline** scales linearly (44.4 -> 1502.7 µs, ~27x at N=32 — the regression), and a **census** shape (leave aliased buffers on the graph-copy path) is flat but slow (~180-210 µs — the large heap blob aborts onto the chunked `CopyTypedDataBaseWithSafepointChecks` slow path and re-lands on the GC heap, the exact cost exp 234 avoids). Table takes baseline's single fast external copy and census's shared-once transport with neither downside, and cuts peak external memory from N buffers to one. Neutral (identical to exp 234) for the overwhelmingly common single-reference write; helps only when a >=256 KB buffer is referenced more than once. Not applicable to reads — a read response's blob cells are distinct objects with no caller aliasing to collapse (see exp 236). Internal knob; adds shared-wrapper unit tests and aliased/coalesced round-trip integration tests.
